text: Teacher caring and teacher support are associated with critical hubs for family-school collaborative interventions targeting adolescent chronic stress, while peer support is associated with the most direct protective factor. Future interventions should prioritize strengthening teacher and peer support and avoid the blind enhancement of coping self-efficacy in uncontrollable family scenarios, thereby providing a solid empirical foundation for collaborative family-school prevention.
source_label: The impact of perceived parental conflict and school protective factors on chronic stress among Chinese adolescents: a network analysis perspective
